title: Module 4: Writing Custom TPU Kernels with Pallas (JAX & TorchTPU Bridge)
description: Writing tile-level TPU kernels in JAX Pallas (VMEM Ref buffers, BlockSpec, register-level bit packing) and calling them inside torch.compile via torch.tpu.pallas.jax_op.

units.title: 4.1 Pallas Programming Model: VMEM Refs, BlockSpec & Grid Pipelining

quiz.question: Inside a JAX Pallas kernel body function, what do the input and output Ref arguments (such as x_ref and o_ref) represent in TPU hardware?
options: Pointers to tiles already staged into on-chip Vector Memory (VMEM) SRAM by the TPU DMA engine according to your BlockSpec.
Global tensors in Host CPU DRAM.
quiz.explanation: Pallas automatically generates async DMA transfers to copy each grid iteration's tile from HBM into on-chip VMEM before invoking your kernel body on x_ref[...] and writing o_ref[...] back to HBM.

units.title: 4.2 Integrating Pallas Kernels into TorchTPU via torch.tpu.pallas.jax_op & LLO Inspection

quiz.question: How does torch.tpu.pallas.jax_op('my_ops::quant_and_pack', quant_and_pack_jax) execute a JAX/Pallas kernel inside a PyTorch torch.compile(backend='tpu') graph?
options: It lowers the JAX/Pallas function to StableHLO, registers it as a native PyTorch custom op with automatic FakeTensor shape inference, and splices the Pallas kernel directly into the TorchTPU XLA graph with zero host copies.
It copies the PyTorch tensor to CPU NumPy on every step.
It rewrites the kernel in CUDA PTX.
quiz.explanation: torch.tpu.pallas.jax_op('namespace::op_name', jax_fn) lowers the JAX/Pallas function directly to StableHLO and registers it in PyTorch's operator dispatcher so TorchDynamo/AOTAutograd fuses it into the TPU binary.
